_comment: Backtest config: the excessive-water-claims automation, live Jul 15 2026 (20% cohort, 26 states). This case already ran playbook steps 5-6 (build the automation, prove it with the alert still on), so it is the machine's proof that the scorecard idea works on a case we lived through. It is an automation-WITHOUT-removal case: the alert still fires and still gates. Sources: MB 131090 (baseline), MB 121562 / 121685 (funnel), bind-rate study wf_f2c194d3 (artifact 3f60f61a), consult-the-book data-recipes.md 'No-touch rate + alert census' and 'Water automation bind-rate impact'.

alert.name: Excessive water claims automation (backtest)
alert.description: The water-claims alert fires ~2,360 times a month by design and kept firing after automation; the system resolves the claims question itself so most quotes never need the underwriter. Live Jul 15 2026 for a 20% slice in 26 states.
notes: Quotes with an un-overridden water alert NEVER bind (zero ever, any period). Comparing automated vs not-automated quotes on bind rate is pure selection; only the launch-states vs control-states comparison is valid.
Automation rate at launch: 231 available, 196 automated (84.8%), 120 needed no UW review at all; of the 76 still reviewed, 74 were caused by a separate non-water alert.

This case shows the growth thesis from the other side: automation alone moved friction (referrals, speed) but NOT binds. Binds move when the gate itself comes off, which water's automation deliberately did not do.

estimator.comparison: the 26 launch states against all other states, before vs after Jul 15 2026, bind windows cut so late-arriving quotes cannot skew either side, with placebo checks on non-water quotes
estimator.notes: Launch states ran hot going into launch (8% to 17% weekly referral swing), so reads carry that caution. Detectable bind effect is +-5pp until ~early Sep 2026.

claims.label: Referral rate on water-only quotes
claims.expectation: If the system does the underwriter's water job, agents stop needing the referral and the rate falls hard.

baseline.unit: % of water-only quotes referred (launch states, pre)
baseline.source: wf_f2c194d3 bind-rate study, launch states pre-launch. The Jan-May all-states baseline definition is 40.6% (MB 131090).
baseline.recipe: db 268: cohort from dbt_upc.uw_alerts_per_quote (alert_id='EXCESSIVE_CLAIMS_WATER', NB, water-only), referrals from eventstore.

actual.unit: % of water-only quotes referred (launch states, post)
actual.source: wf_f2c194d3: 36.5% to 11.9% in launch states while control stayed flat; the gap is far outside noise.

claims.read: The system is doing the underwriter's water job: referrals fell by two thirds where it launched and stayed flat where it did not.

claims.label: Bind rate on water-only quotes
claims.expectation: Automation alone should NOT add binds. The alert still fires and still gates; growth comes only when the gate itself comes off.

actual.unit: pp change in bind rate, launch vs control
actual.source: wf_f2c194d3: 7-day read -2.3pp +-5.4, 14-day read +0.2 to +1.0pp; flat within noise. +-5pp detectable ~early Sep 2026.
actual.recipe: db 268 launch-vs-control comparison, censor-safe bind windows (data-recipes.md, 'Water automation bind-rate impact').

claims.read: Flat, as the thesis says it should be: automation defends, removal unlocks. Water kept its gate, so it bought speed and fewer referrals, not binds.

claims.label: Alert firing volume
claims.expectation: Firing stays flat by design. Alert counts are the wrong scoreboard; underwriter interventions are the right one.

actual.source: Alert census: ~2.36k/mo, flat through launch (data-recipes.md, water automation KPI).
actual.recipe: db 235: dbt.ipod_smga_uw_alerts_per_quote_version, water family, monthly quote-level count.

claims.read: Flat as designed. Anyone reading alert counts as the KPI would call the launch a failure; the referral line says the opposite.

claims.label: Median time to bind, water-only quotes
claims.expectation: Killing the wait shows up as speed even when it does not show up as binds.

actual.source: wf_f2c194d3: 44h to 24h; same-day binds went from 37% to 56% of bound.

claims.read: The friction cost was real: same policies, bound in about half the time.

claims.label: NOC and fix rates on automated binds vs UW-reviewed binds
claims.expectation: If the duplication is faithful, automated binds should draw NOCs and coverage fixes at the same rate the UW-reviewed ones do.

actual.unit: NOCs and UW corrective endorsements per 100 bound, 90 days
actual.denominator: per 100 bound policies of the water-automation cohort, automated vs UW-reviewed lanes, first 90 days after bind
actual.source: NEEDED, not yet readable: launch was Jul 15 and NOCs need ~90 days after bind to show up. First honest read ~mid Oct 2026.
actual.recipe: db 235: rebuild the post-bind census recipe (dbt_dev.damr_uarnoe_* pattern) on the water cohort, automated vs UW-reviewed, once the window closes.

claims.read: This is the claim that matters most for the dwelling-age plan, and it is the one the calendar has not released yet.
